claims.statement: If the L03/leaf04 prime-subfield arithmetic exponent premise holds, one deterministic Turing machine given characteristic c=0 or a promised prime p and rational delta>0 halts with an exact prime-subfield rank-r decomposition of some T_u satisfying r<u^(9/4+delta).
claims.quantifiers: For every rational delta>0 and every c in {0} union the primes, there exists a finite witness; a single exhaustive-search procedure works on all such encoded inputs. The termination proof is conditional on the all-field exponent premise.
claims.interface: Input c and delta in binary; output u,r and complete rational coefficients or residues mod p. The output program embeds into every field of that characteristic. A bit-time evaluator over a field still needs its own exact element representation and operation costs.
claims.proof_or_basis: Stagewise enumerate all candidate u,r and finite coefficient arrays satisfying r^B<u^A, where 9/4+delta=A/B; verify each trilinear identity exactly. The source-derived exponent premise guarantees one accepted finite candidate.
claims.supplied_vs_acquired: The exponent premise is supplied/source-derived; the block witness is acquired by exhaustive search, not supplied. Search time and witness height are not bounded by the source.
claims.costs: Finite total search time conditional on premise. In terms of first-witness maximum dimension/rank/coefficient height S, a simple encoding enumeration is bounded by 2^O(S^4) times polynomial verification, including exact power-comparison bit length O(A log u+B log r) for 9/4+delta=A/B; this need not be polynomial in binary bits(delta). No useful bound S(c,delta) is known here. Exact recurrence arithmetic and coefficient bits remain charged.
claims.matched_baseline: Exact identity verification for a proposed block is polynomial in its finite encoding length; exhaustive candidate discovery is intentionally an unbounded acquisition baseline.
claims.falsifier: A valid c,delta for which the conditional exponent premise holds but no qualifying prime-subfield block witness exists, or a nonterminating/unsound exact candidate verifier.
claims.unresolved_gate: Any useful computable bound on witness size, search time, coefficient height, or practical crossover; primary source does not provide one.

claims.statement: A supplied exact rational Laurent witness with r rank-one terms, factor exponents in [-d,d], and formal identity G(t)=T+O(t) yields rank_Q(T^tensor m)<=r^m(2md+1)^2, with explicit rational coefficient-height and dense output bounds.
claims.quantifiers: For every m>=1 and every witness meeting the stated exact input contract.
claims.interface: Exact Laurent coefficient arrays over Q are supplied. If the witness is acquired rather than supplied, add its acquisition cost. A represented extension E/F of degree k incurs an explicit k^3 descent factor and basis/multiplication-table costs.
claims.proof_or_basis: Expand G(t)^tensor m, take the constant coefficient, and for each of r^m summand words choose exponents u,v; w=-u-v is forced. Rational common denominators give H_m=O(m C H + m H + m log(d+1)) bits per coordinate.
claims.supplied_vs_acquired: Witness supplied in exact symbolic form; no witness finder is claimed by this lemma.
claims.costs: Rank at most r^m(2md+1)^2; dense output has at most that many terms times sum_i n_i^m vector entries; exact construction is output-sensitive and generally exponential in m. Precision is unnecessary for exact input; approximate-only recovery needs a denominator-height bound and exact re-verification.
claims.matched_baseline: Direct formal convolution verifies the supplied identity in O(r n1 n2 n3 d^2) rational operations; no approximation or numerical evaluator is used.
claims.falsifier: An exponent-support or coefficient-extraction error, or an exact rational instance failing the stated rank bound.
claims.unresolved_gate: Compact application to selected outputs and a mask-aware output circuit do not follow from the explicit tensor-power decomposition.

claims.statement: The supplied 2x2x2 W-tensor degeneration has border rank at most 2, exact rank 3, and a standard specialization t=2^-p with cancellation condition Theta(2^p). No exact rank-2 output for W can be extracted from this witness.
claims.quantifiers: One explicit tensor over Q and the stated one-parameter family for all nonzero rational t.
claims.interface: Input the exact Laurent witness; requested output is a rank-2 exact decomposition of W itself.
claims.proof_or_basis: Expansion proves the border-rank witness. The third-mode slice pencil determinant is -x^2; a rank-2 representation forces two independent factors with distinct roots. The two summand norms grow as 1/|t| while the tensor norm stays bounded.
claims.supplied_vs_acquired: The witness is explicitly supplied; no acquisition procedure is involved.
claims.costs: At t=2^-p coefficient encoding has Theta(p) bits; termwise floating-point error bound O(u 2^p) requires about 2p bits to remain below the O(2^-p) approximation error. This is route-specific, not a universal lower bound.
claims.matched_baseline: Three displayed coordinate tensors give exact rank 3. Classical approximate-bilinear/tensor-rank nonclosedness results are primary background.
claims.falsifier: An exact rank-2 decomposition over Q, or an error in the slice-pencil determinant/rank-two factorization argument.
claims.unresolved_gate: Does not rule out another exact algorithm or tensor-power extraction.

claims.statement: The L03 arithmetic exponent and the supplied-witness extraction theorem do not establish a finite-bit O(N^(2-eta)) algorithm for arbitrary supplied W with D=N^(1/4), |W|<=N^(15/8).
claims.quantifiers: Arbitrary N and supplied mask W in the parent program's exact requested-entry interface; no algorithm or general lower bound is claimed.
claims.interface: Dense integer X,Y, exact selected products, supplied arbitrary mask; a bit bound requires an input-bit promise such as b=O(log N).
claims.proof_or_basis: Full product from exponent is O(N^(9/4+epsilon)); direct selected dots cost O(ND+D|W|)=O(N^(17/8)) at maximum mask. Rank alone gives no bound on mask-pruned recursive products, output factor incidence, acquisition, or decoding.
claims.supplied_vs_acquired: Mask W is supplied; a useful mask-aware circuit/output decoder is not acquired by L03 or the border-rank witness.
claims.costs: For b-bit integer inputs, direct input/output representation costs O(ND b + |W|(b+log D)) bits; direct arithmetic uses O(ND+D|W|) integer operations, with the corresponding multiplication bit cost. No subquadratic arbitrary-mask total is proved.
claims.matched_baseline: Direct selected dots; dense rectangular multiplication; exact Cartesian-mask Strassen tiling from Cycle 4 for structured masks only.
claims.falsifier: A complete uniform exact mask-dependent circuit generator with acquisition, coefficient-bit, field-evaluation, shared-arithmetic, output-decoding, and total costs below N^(2-eta).
claims.unresolved_gate: Prove and acquire a mask-aware output-sensitive circuit with bounded coefficient encoding and total subquadratic cost, or prove an interface-matched lower bound.

claims.statement: Over F_2 the functions x^2 and x agree on every field element while the formal polynomial x^2-x is nonzero.
claims.quantifiers: All two inputs in F_2; formal identity in F_2[x].
claims.interface: Any verifier that treats pointwise equality over a finite field as formal polynomial coefficient equality.
claims.proof_or_basis: Evaluate at 0 and 1; the formal polynomial x^2+x has two nonzero coefficients in characteristic 2.
claims.matched_baseline: The family-107 record distinguishes pointwise P.Correct semantics from a stronger coefficient-rank result; no error in that stronger theorem is alleged.
claims.falsifier: A discrepancy in the two evaluations or formal coefficient computation.
claims.unresolved_gate: None for this example; its relevance is limited to specifying verifier semantics.
